_comment: A REMOTE (ADR-012 §1.4): another PBS that PULLS our backups, so a copy of our data lives off-site with them. We grant them a read-only login and nothing more — they hold no write anywhere on our datastore, and we hold no credential on theirs. That asymmetry is what makes the off-site copy survive a compromise here. Created by: backup-manager peer add remote <name>. The login's password is prompted at onboarding and never stored.
name: buddy
_location_note: Where THEIR PBS — the off-site copy of our data — is: a location of this site (site-manager location list); `backup-manager validate` compares it with the site's primary location. peer add --location names it, or --country/--city find or add it. EXAMPLE value.
_namespace_note: What they may read. Empty = the ROOT namespace, i.e. our VM backups. propagate:false keeps the grant off child namespaces — fs/ holds our config and secrets capture, and receive/ holds other peers' data.
_fingerprint_note: They will need our PBS TLS fingerprint and hostname to configure their pull. Onboarding prints both.
_tunnel_note: #796 (BUDDY.md): present when their pull runs over its own WireGuard tunnel, which we SERVE (the pulled side serves). Our PBS is then reachable to them at the tunnel's .1 on tcp/8007 and nowhere else. Written by peer add remote --tunnel serve; e.g. {"role": "serve", "net": "10.255.2.0/30", "listenPort": 51830, "peerKey": "…"}
